lines.text: Hello, I'm Siobhan, one of the physios. What's brought you in?
I'm coming in with a stiff neck and headaches that sit behind my eyes.
Maybe a fortnight ago, maybe longer.
Any tingling or numbness down the arms?

There's been some tingling into my right thumb, which I first noticed when I was up a ladder painting the ceiling, although now that I think about it I'm not totally sure it wasn't my left, and it comes and goes.
Okay. Let me have a look at the neck. Turn your head to the right for me.
Turning right is down to about half, and pressing on the joint at the bottom of the neck on that side brings on the thumb symptoms.
Reflexes and strength in both arms are normal, which is reassuring.
If you get weakness in the hand, or you start dropping things, come back sooner or call 111.
You're going to take paracetamol 1 gram up to four times a day while it's flared.
Thanks, I'll get some on the way home.
Right, that's us. See you in a week, take it easy.
Mr Petrakis? Lovely, come on in. Bit grim out there, isn't it?
Grim isn't the word. Anyway, it's my wrist, I came off my bike on the ice on Monday and it's still really swollen.
